full_judgment: 21. As mentioned earlier, the trial Court after evaluating rent receipts (Exhibits-Kha series and Uma series) and original sale deed dated 9-10-1952 (Exhibit Cha) as well as SA Khatian No. 155 (Exhibit-Chha) and RS Khatian No. 117 (Exhibit-Ja) produced by defendant No. 34 observed that after purchase in 1952 defendant No. 34 has been paying rents of the suit land to the jaminders and thereafter, to the Government which has been upheld by the Court of appeal. Defendant No. 34 produced original sale deed dated 9-10-1952 (Exhibit-Cha) from which it appears that Bashanto Kumar transferred 0.59 acre land and rent receiving interest of 0.23 acre land to defendant No. 34. This sale deed dated 9-10-1952 is more or less admitted by the plaintiff in the way that Bashanto Kumar had no saleable interest to transfer said 0.59 acre land to defendant No. 34 because he was a permissive possessor under the plaintiff. But both the Courts below as well as the Court who passed judgment in the pre-emption case found that the plaintiff or the petitioner in the pre-emption case could not prove the fact of permissive possession. Moreover, sale deed dated 9-10-1952 was attained 30 years of age at the date when it was tendered to evidence on 23-9-1997, original "of which was produced from proper custody and, as such, as per section 90 of the Evidence Act it is to be presumed as genuine document and that the signature and every other part of the document is genuine. As per section 92 of the Evidence Act oral or extraneous evidence to contradict the terms of contents of a document is inadmissible. However, the plaintiff did not adduce any oral or documentary evidence to prove that Exhibit-Cha was a product of forgery. As per recital of sale deed dated 9-10-1952, Bashanto Kumar was a tenant of 0.28 acre land of CS Plot No. 1911 and 0.54 acre land of CS Plot No. 1912 under Putia Jaminder of Rajshahi. The plaintiff was under-tenant from Bashanto Kumar in respect of 0.23 acre land out of 0.54 acre land of CS Plot No. 1912 and Bashanto Kumar transferred entire land of his khas possession and rent receiving interest of 0.23 acre land to defendant No. 34 and handed over possession of 0.28 acre land of CS Plot No. 1911 and 0.31 acre land of CS Plot No. 1912 in favour of defendant No. 34. Since sale deed dated 9-10-1952 is an old document of avove 30 years, as per section 90 read with section 91 of the Evidence Act, the recital of the deed dated 9-10-1952 are presumed to be correct. Moreover, during SA operation said 0.59 acre land was recorded in the name of defendant No. 34 in SA Khatian No. 155 (Exhibit Cha) and 0.23 acre land was recorded in the name of the plaintiff in separate SA Khatian No. 157 (Exhibit-5 Ka) and thereafter, their corresponding RS Khatian No. 117 ( Exhibit-Ja) in respect of 0.59 acre land was prepared and finally published in the name of defendant No. 34 and RS Khatian No. 134 [Exhibit-4 (Kha)] in respect of 0.23 acre land was prepared and finally published in the name of the plaintiff. Moreover, the courts below found that defendant No. 34 paid rent to the Jaminder and Government. The above facts lead to irresistible presumption that the sale deed dated 9-10-1952 has been acted upon. The plaintiff could not produce any evidence to discard the such presumption.
